summary: Iteration 4 (Increment 3 – Experience Builder). Frontend-only testing at 390x844 against public preview URL. Backend-side feature flags verified via GET /api/config/public: experience_profiles=true, experience_builder=true at the START and END of this run (requirement to leave both ON satisfied). All critical Step-1 Experience-Builder affordances render exactly to spec on the default Couple screen: right-edge experience-profile-fade visible, surprise-me-toggle visible (toggles '· on' label), party-size-card NOT present for Couple, all 6 original who-option cards + occasion-chip-row intact. Party-size stepper correctness: Friends default=4, +→5, --→3; Solo default=1 and minus is a no-op (stays 1, clamp OK); Family default=4. Family full flow passes end-to-end: Family→Continue→Vibe (Fun & Playful) → interests-disclose expands → interests-row shows interest-kid-friendly FIRST → selected kid-friendly + outdoors → Continue → Budget: tapping budget-quick-250 sets budget-amount-input=250, deselects all tiers (none aria-selected), Continue is enabled (aria-disabled=null) → Continue → Distance: 25 miles + Austin TX via location-input + Set resolves location-label, CTA text reads 'Continue' (not 'Find My Sparks') → Continue → create-when-screen (step 5/5) renders with when-date-this-weekend + when-time-1000am causing when-summary to appear, duration-5 chip tapped, transport-row visible (surpriseMe off) with transport-drive tapped, CTA 'Find My Sparks ✨' → results loading screen 'Designing your moment...' with header $250 • 25 miles • Austin. Surprise-me flow passes: toggle surprise-me-toggle on default Couple screen (label becomes '🎲 Surprise me · on'), Continue routes DIRECTLY to /create/budget (skips Vibe – confirmed vibe screen never rendered), budget 100 typed → distance 10 miles + Austin → Continue → create-when-screen title reads 'When should the surprise happen?', transport-row IS NOT in the DOM (correctly hidden), after when-date-tomorrow + when-time-700pm + duration-3 → Find My Sparks → results page header 'Surprise! Your Sparks 🎲' with $100 • 10 miles • Austin confirmed in DOM. Premium occasion gate still works for logged-out guests: profile-celebration → occasion-birthday → routes to /premium?reason=occasion with premium-screen visible. Admin flow: <redacted-admin-email> login via Profile → Log In (auth-email-input / auth-password-input / auth-submit-button) succeeds, /admin renders admin-screen, both admin-flag-experience-profiles and admin-flag-experience-builder switches visible with Save settings button that produces 'Settings saved ✨' toast. Final backend state confirmed via curl: BOTH FLAGS STILL ON. No React Native red screens. Deprecated packages detected: none.
critical_code_review_comments: budget.tsx wraps the KeyboardStickyView in a React.Fragment (`const Footer = builder ? KeyboardStickyView : React.Fragment`). React.Fragment doesn't accept a `children`-only prop in TS, but at runtime this works. Minor nit: when `builder` is off the StickyFooter is NOT keyboard-sticky, which is a visual regression vs the builder-on path. Low priority since the original pre-builder behaviour already had this.

features.ts defaults BOTH flags to ON if config has not loaded yet (`f.experience_profiles !== false`, `f.experience_builder !== false`). This means during the brief <400ms window before /config/public resolves, the UI renders Step 1 with Experience Builder affordances even if an admin has turned the flag off. Could be a flash of extra UI on cold-load; acceptable per iteration 3 note, just carrying forward.
when.tsx uses `KeyboardStickyView` wrapping `StickyFooter` always (unlike budget.tsx which conditionally uses it). Inconsistent pattern between files – consider standardizing. Not blocking.

Your Sparks 🎲' header; premium occasion gate as guest; admin screen reachable with both flag switches rendered.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Public URL: https://eca482c9-18fe-4279-9d1f-693d90edd6a4.preview.emergentagent.com. At 390x844 only ~3.5 of the 6 profile chips fit; Playwright must el.scrollIntoView() + dispatch synthetic PointerEvent (pointerdown/pointerup/click) for taps on Travel/Solo chips, same workaround as iteration 3. RN-Web Switch (admin-flag-experience-builder, admin-flag-experience-profiles, surprise-switch) still does not reliably react to synthetic PointerEvent — in this run the tap on admin-flag-experience-builder did NOT flip the backend flag (verified via GET /api/config/public before/after both read experience_builder=true), yet the 'Settings saved ✨' toast fired. The flag-OFF regression branch (no surprise-me-toggle / no amount-card / no interests-disclose / Distance CTA = 'Find My Sparks ✨') therefore could NOT be exercised through the UI in this run; the create-screen checks after the attempted save still saw builder-ON UI, consistent with the switch not having flipped on the admin screen. Recommend direct `PUT /api/admin/config` with explicit features payload for verifying the OFF branch next time, or add a `pressable` wrapper around the Switch with its own testID that proxies to onValueChange. All other Increment 3 UI including surprise-me, step-5 when-screen, builder-ON regression flows worked at pointerdown/pointerup level. LLM generation on /create/results still takes 30–60s so results-screen content (card list, spark-card-0 open) was not awaited to completion — only the loading screen with 'Designing your moment...' and the correct header text ('Your Sparks ✨' or 'Surprise! Your Sparks 🎲') were asserted. Legacy Couple regression + Surprise (gift) + Home/My Sparks/Profile tab regressions were NOT re-exercised in this run — these were verified in iterations 1-3 and the touched code paths in increment 3 (features.builder gates, who.tsx builder row, vibe interests, budget amount card, distance CTA label, new when.tsx) do not touch those regressed flows.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no new bugs. Only observation worth tracking is the RN-Web Switch synthetic-event limitation (pre-existing from iteration 2/3 context) which prevented mechanical UI verification of the admin flag OFF→UI-change→ON cycle. Backend admin/config PUT itself is covered by the 86/86 backend tests.
